subject: geography

sections.title: Practical geography and map work
sections.waec: Part A: map work, statistical maps and diagrams, GIS (GIS is examined for Nigeria only)

topics.title: Map reading: scale, distance, reduction and enlargement
objectives: read and use a map scale to measure distances and areas
reduce and enlarge maps

topics.title: Direction, bearing and representation of relief
objectives: find direction and bearing between places
describe how relief is shown by contours, spot heights and layer colouring

topics.title: Interpretation of physical and cultural features on maps
objectives: identify physical and cultural features on a topographical map
relate features such as settlements and routes to relief and drainage

topics.title: Statistical maps and diagrams
objectives: draw and interpret bar graphs, line graphs, pie charts, dot and choropleth maps
choose a suitable diagram for a given set of data

topics.title: GIS: concepts and components
objectives: define GIS and name its components
give uses of GIS in Nigeria

topics.title: GIS data, satellite remote sensing and applications
objectives: distinguish between vector and raster data
explain how satellite remote sensing supplies geographical data

sections.title: Physical geography
sections.waec: Part A: the earth in space, rocks, tectonic and denudational processes, landforms, weather and climate, climate change (Nigeria only), the environment

topics.title: The earth in space: solar system, rotation, revolution, latitude, longitude and time
objectives: describe the solar system and the earth's shape
explain the effects of rotation and revolution, latitude, longitude and time

topics.title: Structure of the earth and rocks
objectives: describe the structure of the earth
classify rocks as igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic, with Nigerian examples

topics.title: Earth's internal processes: earth movements, vulcanicity and earthquakes
objectives: explain folding, faulting, vulcanicity and earthquakes
describe the landforms they produce

topics.title: Landforms: mountains, plains and lowlands
objectives: describe mountains, plateaux, plains and lowlands
explain how they are formed and used

topics.title: Denudation: weathering and mass movement
objectives: distinguish mechanical, chemical and biological weathering
describe types of mass movement and their effects

topics.title: Running water, groundwater, wind and waves: processes and landforms
objectives: explain how running water, groundwater, wind and waves erode, transport and deposit
describe the landforms each agent produces

topics.title: Weather: elements, instruments and the weather station
objectives: name the elements of weather and the instruments that measure them
describe a weather station and record simple observations

topics.title: Climate: controls, types and classification (Greek and Köppen)
objectives: explain the controls of climate
describe the Greek and Köppen classifications of climate

topics.title: Climate change
objectives: explain the causes and evidence of climate change
describe its effects on Nigeria and ways of adapting and reducing it

topics.title: Environmental resources: renewable and non-renewable
objectives: classify environmental resources as renewable and non-renewable
explain their importance and how to manage them

topics.title: Environmental problems, hazards and conservation
objectives: describe environmental hazards and problems and their causes
explain methods of conservation

sections.title: Human and economic geography
sections.waec: Part B: world population, settlement, transportation, industry, trade, tourism

topics.title: World population
objectives: describe world population distribution, growth and structure
explain the factors that affect them

topics.title: Settlement: rural and urban, functions and interactions
objectives: classify rural and urban settlements and their functions
explain settlement interactions

topics.title: Transportation
objectives: compare modes of transport and their roles in development
explain problems of transport in developing countries

topics.title: Industry
objectives: classify industries
explain factors of industrial location with world examples

topics.title: Trade
objectives: distinguish internal and international trade
explain the factors and problems of trade

topics.title: Tourism
objectives: explain the importance of tourism
describe tourist attractions and the problems of tourism

sections.title: Regional geography of Nigeria
sections.waec: Part C (Nigeria): broad outline, physical setting, population, resources, agriculture, transportation, communication, industry, trade, tourism, development and environmental issues, ECOWAS, geopolitical issues

topics.title: Location and Physical Setting of Nigeria
objectives: state the location of Nigeria using latitude and longitude, and name its neighbours
describe Nigeria's size and its political divisions
identify the main relief regions of Nigeria and give examples of each

topics.title: Climate of Nigeria
objectives: distinguish weather from climate, name the instruments of a weather station and explain the main controls of Nigeria's climate
name the two air masses that control Nigeria's seasons and describe each one
explain how the movement of the Inter-Tropical Discontinuity (ITD) causes the wet and dry seasons

topics.title: Vegetation and Soils of Nigeria
objectives: describe the main vegetation belts of Nigeria and the factors that control them
describe the characteristics and uses of each vegetation belt
explain how soils form and describe a soil profile

topics.title: Population and Settlement
objectives: state Nigeria's population size and explain how it is measured
describe and explain the distribution of population in Nigeria
discuss the effects of rapid population growth and migration

topics.title: Natural Resources and Agriculture
objectives: classify natural resources as renewable or non-renewable, with examples
locate Nigeria's main mineral resources and explain their importance
describe the main types of agriculture practised in Nigeria

topics.title: Transport, Communication and Industrial Development
objectives: describe the main modes of transport in Nigeria and their advantages and problems
identify major seaports, airports and railway lines
explain the importance of communication networks

topics.title: Trade, Tourism and Environmental Issues
objectives: distinguish between internal (domestic) and international trade and describe Nigeria's main exports and imports
explain the importance of trade and the role of ECOWAS
identify major tourist attractions and explain the importance and problems of tourism

topics.title: ECOWAS
objectives: state the aims and member states of ECOWAS
evaluate its achievements and problems

topics.title: Geopolitical issues
objectives: explain Nigeria's geopolitical zones and boundary issues
discuss the geography of resource control and regional development

topics.title: Local geography: your town or village and local government area
objectives: describe the physical and human features of the local area
carry out simple observations of the immediate environment

sections.title: Fieldwork
sections.waec: Part D: one fieldwork study (land use, market survey, traffic flow, journey to work or local erosion), assessed in school

topics.title: Planning and reporting a fieldwork study
objectives: plan a fieldwork study with an aim and methods
collect, present and analyse field data in a report

not_for_nigeria: Elementary surveying, hydrosphere, vegetation and soil (as world topics) are marked in the WAEC syllabus for Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia and The Gambia. Nigeria's vegetation and soils are covered in Lesson 3 as part of Nigeria's physical setting.
The regional geography of Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Senegambia and the selected topics on Africa are examined for those countries, not for Nigerian candidates.
level_note: Class levels follow NERDC-based schemes of work (they differ between schools and between the older and the 2025/26 curriculum). Every topic is examined in WASSCE at the end of SSS 3.

objective: Read the whole question and every option before choosing; underline key words such as NOT, BEST or MAIN.
Eliminate options you know are wrong, then choose between the rest.
For calculations, write the formula and the units, and check that the answer is sensible.
Do not spend too long on one question; mark it and return to it if time allows.
Answer every question: a blank answer cannot earn a mark.
structured: Look at the command word: 'name' or 'state' needs a short answer; 'describe' needs details; 'explain' needs reasons; 'account for' needs causes.
Use the marks as a guide: a 6-mark part usually needs about three well-developed points.
Support each point with a named Nigerian example (a place, state, river or figure with its year).
Use clear sketch maps and labelled diagrams where they help; give them a title and a key.
Write in short paragraphs, one point per paragraph, and keep to the question asked.
exam_guidance.note: These are general study strategies. No question is guaranteed to appear in any examination.
